sections.title: Current official requirement
sections.body: UCL’s current Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD prospectus states that applicants normally need an upper-second-class UK integrated Master’s (MSci/MPhys) in a relevant discipline, an undergraduate degree followed by a relevant MSc, or an overseas equivalent. It also says an upper-second/first-class Bachelor’s or equivalent may be considered only in special circumstances. UCL further states that the course will not accept applicants qualified only to Bachelor’s level and generally seeks the equivalent of a good UK Master’s by enrolment. citeturn0view0

sections.title: Applicant-to-requirement reconciliation
sections.body: Subject prerequisite: SATISFIED on the supplied record. Amara has a BSc in Physics, advanced physics coursework including quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, statistical mechanics, nuclear and particle physics, and computational physics, plus detector-reconstruction research at CERN OpenLab. This is directly relevant to the programme’s Physics/High Energy Particle Physics pathway, which UCL lists among its research groups. citeturn0view0turn1view2

sections.title: Academic-level prerequisite
sections.body: NOT SATISFIED under the normal stated route, based on the supplied materials. The record shows a BSc Physics completed and conferred in 2024, with no MSc, MSci, MPhys, or other postgraduate qualification. The CGPA of 4.62/5.00 is strong, but the materials do not establish that it is an overseas equivalent of the required UK Master’s-level qualification. UCL’s Bachelor’s-only exception is discretionary (‘may be considered in special circumstances’), so eligibility through that exception cannot be verified without UCL’s assessment or additional official equivalency evidence. citeturn0view0

sections.title: Other consequential checks
sections.body:
English-language requirement: unresolved. The current prospectus specifies UCL English Language Level 1, but the materials contain no accepted test result, exemption evidence, or confirmation that the applicant satisfies that level. citeturn0view0

Supervisor/admissions contact: required as an application-preparation expectation, not a stated academic qualification. The current prospectus says applicants should in most cases identify and contact potential supervisors; the department page specifically instructs applicants to contact at least one relevant admissions tutor and to approach an appropriate academic in advance. No such contact is evidenced in the materials. citeturn0view0turn1view2

References: two are required. Professor Ifeanyi Eze is the strongest confirmed academic referee because he taught Amara and supervised her final-year project. Dr Sofia Marin is a plausible professional/research referee. Mr Kunle Aina is weaker because his eight-week internship supervision did not include academic work. UCL requires at least one academic reference from someone who taught the applicant at degree level when two references are required. citeturn0view0turn1view1

sections.title: Stale or conflicting programme information
sections.body: The department page contains older entry-cycle information referring to 2025–2026 start dates and older funding wording. The current prospectus is dated for the 2026/27 fee and 2026–2027 entry cycle, lists rolling applications with submission at least three months before the preferred start date, and should control for the current prerequisite assessment. The department page remains useful for research-group and contact expectations, but its old cycle-specific dates should not be treated as current. citeturn0view0turn1view2

sections.title: What cannot be verified
sections.body: I cannot verify that Amara qualifies for the Bachelor’s-level special-circumstances exception; that her Nigerian BSc is formally equivalent to UCL’s required standard; that she satisfies English Level 1; that a supervisor has agreed to consider the project; or that full tuition plus living-stipend funding is available for her specific application. UCL lists funding routes and limited scholarships, but the supplied sources do not establish an award for this applicant. citeturn0view0turn1view2

sections.title: Bottom line
sections.body: Amara is a strong subject fit for particle-physics research, but on the evidence provided she is not currently verified as meeting UCL’s normal academic prerequisite because she has only a Bachelor’s degree. The application would depend on UCL accepting her under the discretionary special-circumstances route or on obtaining a relevant postgraduate qualification. The next decisive evidence would be written confirmation from UCL Physics/Graduate Admissions about whether her BSc and profile can be considered under that exception, plus accepted English-language evidence if required.

follow_ups: Obtain written UCL confirmation on the Bachelor’s-level special-circumstances route and overseas qualification equivalence.
Provide an accepted English-language result or documented exemption.
If proceeding, identify a relevant HEP supervisor/admissions tutor and preserve the correspondence.
